 Rui Hachimura (quad) is not on the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Heat. 
 Hachimura did not play in Monday’s loss to the Raptors, as Kobe Sanders moved into the starting lineup and scored a career-high 26 points. Sanders will return to the bench, which significantly limits his fantasy value.

 Rui Hachimura accumulated 21 points (7-of-18 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), nine rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat. 
 Hachimura has gotten off to a relatively slow start with the Clippers, shooting 37.3 percent from the field and 68.4 percent from the foul line. Add inconsistent production in assists, steals and blocks, and rostering Hachimura in some 10-team leagues isn’t worth discussing. He had a productive night against the Heat, with the seven assists being more than double his total entering the night (three). For Hachimura to be someone you can roster in shallow leagues after the Clippers get guys like Brandon Ingram and Bradley Beal back, nights like Wednesday have to become the norm. 
 Derrick Jones 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #5 
 Darius Garland, Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr., Rui Hachimura and Brook Lopez will start Wednesday’s game against the Heat. 
 Jones and Hachimura are available after missing Monday’s loss to the Raptors. As a result, Gradey Dick and Kobe Sanders will come off the bench. 
 Kobe Sanders 
 LAC 
 Guard 
 #4 
 Kobe Sanders produced 26 points (8-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one block and five three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Raptors. 
 The Clippers didn’t have Derrick Jones Jr. or Rui Hachimura for Monday’s game, so Sanders made his second start of the season. The second-year wing had the best night of his NBA career, dropping a career-high 26 points. Sanders scored 13 points in both halves, but he may have run out of steam late. Shooting 1-of-5 from the field, Sanders scored five points in the fourth quarter, and the Clippers shot 30.4 percent as a team. That’s how a team goes from leading by 13 to losing by seven. 
 Gradey Dick 
 LAC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #9 
 Darius Garland, Gradey Dick, Kris Dunn, Kobe Sanders and Brook Lopez will start Monday’s game against the Raptors. 
 The Clippers are down three starters for Monday’s game, with Rui Hachimura, Derrick Jones Jr. and Isaiah Jackson unavailable. They’ve been replaced in the lineup by Gradey, Sanders and Lopez. Of the three, Lopez may be the safest option for fantasy managers. 
 Rui Hachimura 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #28 
 Rui Hachimura (quad) is out for Monday’s game against the Raptors. 
 Hachimura is coming off a 24-point game in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors, but he’ll sit out the second night of a back-to-back against the Raptors Monday. With Hachimura sidelined with left quad soreness, Kobe Sanders could move into the starting lineup. 
 Derrick Jones 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #5 
 Derrick Jones Jr. (knee) finished Sunday’s loss to the Warriors with nine points (3-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer. 
 Jones exited Sunday’s game late in the third quarter with a sore knee and did not return. That casts some doubt on his availability for Monday’s game against the Raptors. If Jones can’t play, Kobe Sanders may move into the starting lineup. 
 Kobe Sanders 
 LAC 
 Guard 
 #4 
 Kobe Sanders amassed 16 points (6-of-9 FGs), three rebounds, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors. 
 Sanders had his most productive game of the season so far, setting new highs in points and three-pointers. He’s now played at least 20 minutes in four straight games, logging 30 against the Warriors. Sunday’s performance isn’t enough to get him on the radar in most fantasy leagues, but it may ensure Sanders a place in head coach Tyronn Lue’s rotation while the Clippers await the returns of Brandon Ingram and Max Strus. 
 Rui Hachimura 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #28 
 Rui Hachimura accounted for 24 points (10-of-16 FGs), seven rebounds and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Warriors. 
 Hachimura had a good offensive night against the Warriors, but his final stat line reminded fantasy managers not to expect much beyond points, rebounds and three-pointers. In 30 minutes, Hachimura shot well over 50 percent from the field but did not record an assist, steal or blocked shot. The Clippers play three games next week, starting with the Raptors on Monday. 
 Rui Hachimura 
 LAC 
 Forward 
 #28 
 Rui Hachimura accounted for 12 points (4-of-11 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves. 
 Back in the Clippers’ lineup after missing Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers, Hachimura played 26 minutes against the Timberwolves. He didn’t shoot well, but Rui recorded a few steals in his return. Kobe Sanders, who started on Wednesday, finished with seven points, four rebounds and two steals in 24 minutes off the bench. The Clippers play one more game this week, Sunday night against the Warriors.

 Hachimura is back after a one-game absence and will return to his usual starting role. As a result, Kobe Sanders, who started Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers, is back on the bench.

 Brook Lopez amassed 20 points (8-of-11 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist, two blocks and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat.
 After playing 22 minutes in his first start of the season on Monday, Lopez played 35 in Wednesday’s overtime thriller. Given his production in those two starts and Isaiah Jackson’s inability to avoid silly fouls, Lopez may have the starting center job for the foreseeable future. Jackson, who has committed at least four fouls in six of his eight games, played 13 minutes against the Heat and finished with two points, four rebounds, two assists and one steal.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo recorded 27 points (8-of-20 FGs, 11-of-13 FTs), 14 rebounds, six assists, two steals and three blocks in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 On most nights, fantasy managers can expect Giannis to shoot a high percentage from the field but struggle at the foul line. The opposite happened against the Clippers, with the Heat forward shooting 40 percent from the field and 84.6 percent from the foul line. Antetokounmpo finished with a robust stat line that had everything but a three-pointer. The Heat play two more games this week, starting with the Warriors on Thursday.

 Davion Mitchell tallied 11 points (5-of-13 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, 10 assists, four steals and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 Mitchell’s start to the season has been better than most fantasy managers expected, with the Heat guard providing top-50 per-game value. He couldn’t buy a three-pointer on Wednesday, missing all five attempts, but Mitchell offered excellent production in assists and steals. And even with Wednesday’s poor shooting, Mitchell is still shooting 50 percent from the field this season.

 Bam Adebayo recorded 35 points (14-of-20 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 This was a big night for Adebayo, who recorded his first double-double of the season with new highs in points and rebounds. Add in the assists, and it was a good night for those rostering the Heat captain. Even with there still being some bumps the Heat need to smooth over as they work Giannis Antetokounmpo into the fold, Adebayo has been close to a top-25 player in 12-team leagues. That’s encouraging, to say the least.

 Klay Thompson finished Wednesday’s overtime win over the Clippers with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and eight three-pointers.
 Thompson had his best game of the season on Wednesday, shooting 8-of-17 from beyond the arc. His last three-pointer was the most important, as the Heat guard/forward hit one from the left corner with one second remaining in overtime to give Miami the win. Inconsistent in his first five games, Thompson has scored at least 19 points in three straight. Could he be returning to fantasy relevance? The Heat play two more games this week, so it may not be a bad time to stream Klay if you need three-pointers. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Naji Marshall produced 22 points (9-of-12 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs.
 The Mavericks had no answer for Victor Wembanyama and looked set to get blown out. However, Marshall got going in the second half, shooting 7-of-9 from the field and scoring 17 points. Marshall remains a player who can be rostered in deep leagues, even though he’ll come off the bench on most nights.

 Cooper Flagg finished Wednesday’s loss to the Spurs with 19 points (7-of-19 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), 10 rebounds and five assists.
 After shooting 3-of-19 from the field in Monday’s loss to the Kings, Flagg got off to a terribly slow start on Wednesday. The reigning Rookie of the Year missed all seven of his shots in the first quarter and started 1-of-11 from the field. The good news is that Flagg shot 6-of-8 the rest of the way. Add in the rebounds and assists, and the final stat line was solid, but category managers would have wanted to see more defensive stats.
